column2: Radius: distance from the centre of the circle to any point on the circle
Circumference: perimeter of a circle = 2πr
Chord: a line segment joining two points on a circle
Diameter: the longest chord, always passes through the centre = 2r
Secant: a line that cuts a circle at two points
Tangent: a line that touches the circle at one point and is perpendicular to the radius there
Arc: the curved path of the circle between two points on it
Segment: the region of a circle bounded by a chord and its corresponding arc
Sector: the region enclosed between two radii and the arc between them
Concentric circles: circles having the same centre
Congruent circles: circles having equal radii
Congruent arcs: arcs with equal radii and equal central angles
Subtended angles of an arc: angle at centre, angle at circle
Angle relation: angle at centre = 2 × angle at the circle
Shortest distance from a point to a line is the length of the perpendicular from the point to the line
Chord subtended angles in the same segment of a circle are equal

column3: If two chords subtend equal angles at the centre or at the circle, then the chords are equal
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre
Chords equidistant from the centre are equal in length
If two chords are equal, their corresponding arcs are congruent
If two arcs are congruent, their corresponding chords are equal
Congruent arcs subtend equal angles at the centre
Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre
If a line segment makes equal angles at two points on the same side of the line, then the four points lie on the same circle

column2: Chord-subtended angles in opposite segments of a circle are supplementary
Angle subtended by a chord at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at the circle
